answer: A new agent must lock a bond and publish a public cipher of a secret it will later reveal from its trade diary. For three epochs it may transact only with a small, randomly assigned island of incumbents. Each incumbent adds one signed stanza, and the fourteen stanzas form a sonnet folded into the next cipher. When the secret is opened, if the diary, the sonnet, and the cipher disagree, or if those incumbents later prove they were paid from the same purse, the bond is slashed and the name is burned. Fake swarms fail together, because one purse cannot honestly fill many disjoint islands.
